issues.problem: The two characters are only about 60-80 px tall and their dark navy/brown bodies merge into the brown path, so at 720p JPEG they read a beat slower than the cabin and trees do.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 2 '10 looks like': subject clear within 1 s at 720p; §4.1 minor flaw 0.2
issues.fix: Add a 1-2 px lighter rim outline (e.g. warm cream #F3E2C0 at 60%) around the characters, or zoom the camera about 10% closer to the fire

issues.problem: The cabin window interiors are a near-black flat fill, darker and less tinted than the rest of the warm palette.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 3 '10 looks like': no pure black, tinted shadows; §4.1 minor flaw 0.1
issues.fix: Lift the window fill to a warm deep plum such as #3A2A3A and add a single warm-lit pane highlight

issues.region: characters, logs and fence at mid-frame
issues.problem: The key light gives very little lift: the characters and fence posts have small, faint ground shadows, so they sit on the ground instead of lifting off it the way the cabin and trees do.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 4: pieces lift off through shadow or rim light; §4.1 minor flaw 0.2
issues.fix: Darken the blob shadows under the characters and posts by about 15% and offset them 2-3 px down-right, away from the upper-left key

issues.region: upper-centre and right, red and orange autumn trees
issues.problem: The large saturated red canopies above and right of the fire are about as loud as the campfire, so the focal point is shared on a second look.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 6: one obvious focal point; §4.1 minor flaw 0.2
issues.fix: Desaturate the peripheral red canopies by about 10% or warm up the fire glow radius (a soft 80 px additive falloff) so the fire wins

issues.region: bottom edge, grey boulder and teal pool (~x660-1110, y530-720)
issues.problem: The large boulder and pool are hard-cropped by the bottom frame edge, and the fence curve makes a tangent with the rock top, which leaves a heavy, awkward mass in the lower third.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 7 '≤ 5' column: awkward tangents (a deliberate crop is allowed); §4.1 minor flaw 0.2
issues.fix: Tilt the camera up about 40 px so the rock sits below the frame or shows its full crest, which clears the fence and rock tangent

issues.region: cliff rock faces, top-left and top-right
issues.problem: The striated rock texture repeats a similar horizontal dash pattern across the cliff faces, which is slightly noticeable on a second look.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 10: no visible tiling; §4.1 minor flaw 0.1
issues.fix: Vary the stripe length and spacing on the rock tiles, or add 2-3 variants rotated at random per face

issues.region: mid-frame, thin yellow line from cabin roof across to right edge (~y290-520)
issues.problem: A 1 px bright yellow diagonal line crosses the scene from the cabin to the right edge and reads as a stray line or seam artefact rather than an object.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 18: no seams or visible artefacts; §4.1 minor flaw 0.2
issues.fix: If it is a gameplay guide line, give it a 2 px softened alpha 0.5 treatment with end caps; if not, remove it from the render layer

issues.problem: The two characters are only about 40-50 px tall and the dark-blue figure sits on dark soil, so on a second look they read less instantly than the cabin and red trees at 720p.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 2 (subject clear within 1 s at 720p); §4.1 reference-band minor, 0.2
issues.fix: Add a 1-2 px warm light rim/outline to the characters from the fire, or push the camera in about 10% so the figures reach about 60 px tall.

issues.problem: The cabin windows are near-black purple, the one value that breaks the otherwise warm, tinted palette.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 3 (no pure black; tinted shadows); §4.1 minor, 0.1
issues.fix: Lift the window fill to a warm deep plum, around #3a2a3a, with a faint amber interior glow.

issues.problem: The fire, which should be the key warm light, casts almost no glow on the nearby ground or figures, so the lighting reads as flat ambient light around the focal point.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 4 (pieces lift off through lighting); §4.1 minor, 0.2
issues.fix: Add a soft radial warm glow (about 120 px radius, orange at 15-20% alpha) around the fire, plus small contact shadows under the figures.

issues.problem: The signboard posts are thin and spindly compared with the chunky cabin and fence.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 5 (chunky toy silhouettes); §4.1 minor, 0.1
issues.fix: Make the sign posts about 2 px wider and round the board corners by 1 px step.

issues.region: upper-centre and right, red and yellow autumn trees
issues.problem: The saturated red-orange canopies above the campfire compete with the fire for the eye's first stop.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 6 (one obvious focal point); §4.1 minor, 0.2
issues.fix: Desaturate the canopies directly above the fire by about 10% or darken them slightly, so the fire stays the brightest warm accent.

issues.region: bottom-right, fence meeting the rock and water
issues.problem: The end of the fence forms a tangent with the grey boulder rim, and the teal pool is cut off at the bottom edge.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 7 (awkward tangents); §4.1 minor, 0.2
issues.fix: Shift the camera up about 40 px, or end the fence 20 px before the boulder, so the fence and rock separate and the pool reads as a deliberate crop.

issues.problem: The waterfall is cropped awkwardly at the top edge, leaving a sliver that pulls the eye to the corner.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 7 (breathing room, no awkward crops); §4.1 minor, 0.1
issues.fix: Crop the waterfall fully out, or include at least 60 px more of it.

issues.problem: The striated rock texture repeats similar horizontal stroke patterns across the top-left cliff.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 10 (no visible tiling); §4.1 minor, 0.1
issues.fix: Vary the stroke length and add 2-3 unique crack or moss details to break up the repeating pattern.

issues.problem: The premium feel holds, but the fire focal point lacks a glow or particle payoff, which slightly undersells the cozy central moment.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 15 (premium indie gut check); §4.1 minor, 0.1
issues.fix: Add a warm fire glow and 3-5 ember pixels rising with the smoke.

issues.region: thin light lines crossing the centre and right (~380-1250 x 370-520)
issues.problem: Faint one-pixel diagonal yellow lines cross the scene and can read as rendering seams rather than intentional rope or light.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 18 (no seams or artefacts); §4.1 minor, 0.2
issues.fix: Either give the lines clear anchors and a 2 px width so they read as intentional, or remove them.

issues.problem: The white wind-trail arcs are drawn as thin 2 px anti-aliased vector strokes. They don't sit on the chunky pixel grid used everywhere else, so they read as a second rendering style.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 1 (one cohesive art direction), reference band minor flaw
issues.fix: Draw the wind arcs on the same pixel grid as the art (about 4 px steps at this scale, no sub-pixel anti-aliasing), or snap the stroke to the world pixel size

issues.region: upper-centre and right-centre yellow orb clusters
issues.problem: The yellow bokeh/light orbs are soft, round, low-alpha discs whose edges don't match the hard-edged pixel foliage. On a second look they read as a filter pasted over the art.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 1, reference band minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Quantise the orbs to pixel-grid dithered circles in 2-3 palette steps instead of smooth alpha discs

issues.problem: The navy/red character is only about 80 px wide and sits on dark mid-green foliage and orange trunk, with little value contrast. At 720p stream compression the subject takes a moment to find.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 2 (subject reads instantly at 720p), reference band minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Add a 1-pixel light rim or outline in a warm cream (#F3E6C8-ish) around the character sprite, or lift the value of the ground patch under it by about 15% L

issues.problem: The waterfall's near-white foam is the highest-contrast area in the frame and pulls the eye away from the subject on a stream thumbnail.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 2, reference band minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Tone the foam highlight down to a pale tinted aqua (about #DDF3EE) and keep peak white only for tiny sparkle pixels

issues.problem: The foam uses large areas of close-to-pure white, the only untinted value in an otherwise warm, harmonised palette.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 3 (no pure black or white), reference band minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Replace the #FFFFFF-range foam with a tinted off-white (about #EAF7F2) and keep it within the aqua ramp

issues.problem: The diagonal yellow light shaft sets up a key light from the lower right, but the character casts no matching shadow and has no rim, so it doesn't lift off the ground as much as the trees do.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 4 (pieces lift off through rim light plus shadow, judged in principle)
issues.fix: Add a 2-3 px offset darker-green drop/blob shadow under the character opposite the key, plus a 1 px warm highlight on the key-facing edge

issues.problem: The yellow light-ray lines are thin single strokes and barely read as volumetric light, which makes the lighting direction ambiguous at a glance.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 4, reference band minor flaw (0.1)
issues.fix: Widen the shaft into 2-3 banded dithered strips at 10-20% opacity rather than 1-2 px lines

issues.problem: A few foreground pine crowns end in long, sharp single-pixel spikes. They're slightly spindlier than the chunky canopy shapes used elsewhere.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 5 (chunky silhouettes), reference band minor flaw (0.1)
issues.fix: Blunt the pine tips to 2x2 pixel ends and round the lowest tier of each crown by one pixel step

issues.problem: The bright waterfall and the busy yellow orb clusters compete with the central character, so the eye's path splits for a moment before it lands on the subject.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 6 (one obvious focal point), reference band minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Reduce the waterfall foam's peak value by about 10% and cut orb density near the edges by about 30%, keeping the brightest orbs clustered near the character

issues.problem: A vertical column of bright orbs at the right creates a secondary hotspot that has no gameplay meaning.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 6, reference band minor flaw (0.1)
issues.fix: Break the column up, lower orb alpha to about 60% there, or tint the orbs toward the surrounding green

issues.region: bottom edge centre (bridge at x 550-640, y 690-720)
issues.problem: The bridge runs straight into the bottom frame edge, making a tangent that pins the lower composition.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 7 (awkward tangents), reference band minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Pan the camera down about 40 px, or let the bridge turn or end on land before the frame edge

issues.problem: The dark olive grass circles repeat in near-identical size and spacing, so the ground texture reads a little like a stamp.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 10 (no visible tiling), reference band minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Vary the tuft stamps' size (±30%), rotation and spacing, and mix in 2-3 alternative tuft shapes

issues.problem: It reads as premium, but the smooth anti-aliased overlays (orbs, wind strokes, ray lines) sitting on crisp pixel art slightly weaken the shipped-product impression.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 15 (stranger believes premium indie), reference band minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Unify all FX layers on the pixel grid (see CAL-R1-01/02/07) so every overlay shares the base art's resolution

issues.region: orb clusters and wind arcs, centre
issues.problem: The soft orb edges and anti-aliased strokes create mixed-resolution fringing against the hard pixel edges, which reads as a faint scaling artefact.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 18 (no aliasing/visible artefacts), reference band minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Render FX at the art's native pixel resolution and upscale with nearest-neighbour together with the base layer

issues.region: centre and left 40% (white wind arcs over character and waterfall)
issues.problem: The white wind/motion arcs are smooth, anti-aliased vector strokes sitting on top of chunky pixel art, which breaks the single-resolution pixel language a little.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 1: one cohesive art direction; §4.1 reference-band minor flaw (-0.2)
issues.fix: Draw the arcs on the same pixel grid (1 art-pixel wide, 2-3 stepped segments, no AA) or snap them to the native art resolution before upscaling.

issues.problem: The player character is only about 70x40 px and dark navy against busy dark-green foliage, so it takes a moment to find at 720p.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 2: subject reads instantly at 720p; §4.1 minor (-0.2)
issues.fix: Add a 1-art-pixel warm light rim or a soft light pool under the character, or push the local foliage value about 15% darker or lighter to separate it.

issues.problem: The dense yellow out-of-focus discs add high-frequency clutter around the subject, which hurts readability after JPEG compression.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 2 stream readability; §4.1 minor (-0.2)
issues.fix: Cut the bokeh disc count by about 40% within 150 px of the character and drop their opacity from about 80% to 50%.

issues.problem: The waterfall foam is close to pure white, the one untinted value in an otherwise warm, harmonised palette.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 3: no pure white; §4.1 minor (-0.2)
issues.fix: Tint the foam highlight to a pale aqua-cream (e.g. #F2FAF4) to match the scene's warm key.

issues.problem: The single hard, thin yellow light-ray line reads like a stray line more than a sunbeam, which weakens an otherwise soft dappled-light model.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 4 lighting; §4.1 minor (-0.2)
issues.fix: Widen the ray to a 12-20 px additive soft band at about 25% opacity, or remove it and rely on the dappled canopy light.

issues.problem: Some grey rock outlines have jagged, stair-stepped contours that are harsher than the soft, rounded canopy shapes.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 5 form softness; §4.1 minor (-0.1)
issues.fix: Smooth the rock silhouettes with 2-step pixel curves and a darker 1-art-pixel inner shade to round them.

issues.problem: The bright waterfall on the left has the highest contrast in the frame and competes with the central character for first fixation.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 6: one obvious focal point; §4.1 minor (-0.2)
issues.fix: Lower the waterfall's peak brightness by about 10% or add a gentle vignette on the left third so the eye lands on the character first.

issues.problem: Busy foliage and yellow discs right around the subject diffuse focus a little.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 6 hierarchy; §4.1 minor (-0.1)
issues.fix: Lower local detail contrast in a 120 px radius around the character (desaturate foliage about 10%).

issues.problem: The bridge's lower end runs straight into the bottom frame edge and makes a tangent, and a trunk grazes the top-right corner.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 7: no awkward tangents; §4.1 minor (-0.2)
issues.fix: Move the camera up about 40 px so the bridge's end sits in frame, or let it cross the edge on a diagonal.

issues.problem: The depth-of-field blur on the foreground grass turns the pixel texture into mush that reads as a soft upscale, not as a material.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 10: no blurry art; §4.1 minor (-0.2)
issues.fix: Replace the Gaussian blur with a lower-detail hand-pixelled foreground layer, or cap the blur radius at 1 art-pixel.

issues.problem: Mixed-resolution effects (smooth strokes and Gaussian blur on pixel art) are the one tell that keeps it just short of flawless premium polish.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 15 AAA gut check; §4.1 minor (-0.1)
issues.fix: Render all post-effects (wind lines, DOF, rays) at the native pixel resolution before the integer upscale.

issues.problem: The anti-aliased arcs and the blur on top of nearest-neighbour pixels give visible mixed-resolution edges.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 18 technical cleanliness; §4.1 minor (-0.2)
issues.fix: Snap overlay effects to the art-pixel grid and apply the upscale last.

issues.problem: The bokeh discs have soft, smooth edges that clash with the hard pixel edges beside them.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 18; §4.1 minor (-0.1)
issues.fix: Draw the bokeh as dithered pixel discs at native resolution.

issues.problem: There is no art direction. The pieces, board and background are untextured default Lambert/grey materials on a flat #808080 clear colour, the UI is browser-default serif text and stock buttons, and nothing reads as a clay, wood or paper world.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 1 ≤5 column: default grey three.js materials, stock widgets; §4.1 anchor 5
issues.fix: Swap all MeshLambert/Standard defaults for one handcrafted material set (warm wood board with felt inlay, clay-roughness 0.8 pieces), put the board in a room or backdrop scene instead of the grey clear colour, and restyle all UI as paper cards in one font family

issues.problem: The turn, score and room code sit in about 16 px black Times text jammed into the corner. At stream quality you have to squint to find whose turn it is, and nothing in the scene marks the active player (P2).
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 2: turn/state/scores clear within 1 s, critical text ≥22 px at 1080p; ≤5: squinting required
issues.fix: Add a turn banner at the top centre (≥32 px at 1080p) coloured in the active player's identity colour, a score strip with per-player chips at ≥24 px, and a glow ring under the active player's pieces

issues.region: piece clusters in all four corners
issues.problem: Pure primary red, green, blue and yellow (roughly #CC0000/#00CC00/#0000CC/#CCCC00) sit on neutral greys. Shadows are grey and untinted, and nothing is harmonised or saturation-controlled.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 3 ≤5: off-palette, grey shadows; §4.1 anchor 5 'primary colours'
issues.fix: Replace them with a harmonised muted set (e.g. terracotta #D9745B, sage #7FA36B, dusk blue #5B7FB8, honey #E3B64F), tint the shadows warm violet (#4A3B55 at 35%) and swap the grey background for a warm tinted environment

issues.problem: Flat directional lighting with no cast or contact shadows, so the pieces float on the board. There is no rim light, no mood and no mode identity.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 4 ≤5: flat or harsh lighting
issues.fix: Add an upper-left warm key (intensity 1.2, 4500K) with soft PCF shadows, a cool fill at 0.3, a rim light from behind, and blob contact shadows (radius 1.2× the piece, 40% opacity) under each piece

issues.problem: The die is a sharp-edged box, the board is a zero-thickness plane with hard edges, and the cylinders have unbeveled rims. There are no chunky toy silhouettes.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 5 ≤5: sharp boxes
issues.fix: Use RoundedBoxGeometry (radius 0.12) for the die with pips, give the board 0.3 units of thickness with a 0.08 bevel, and lathe the pieces into rounded pawn or meeple shapes with a 0.1 fillet

issues.problem: There is no focal point. The grey sphere and cube in the centre are ambiguous, and the call to action (the Roll button) is a tiny stock button in the corner. The eye has no action → state → context path.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 6 ≤5: unclear call to action
issues.fix: Make Roll a large primary button at the bottom centre (≥56 px tall, identity-coloured, drop shadow) with the die hovering above it, give the active player's quadrant a highlight, and dim the idle pieces by 20%

issues.problem: The board runs off-balance toward the bottom edge, which is nearly tangent to it, leaving a large dead grey band at the top. The UI crowds the corners.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 7 ≤5: awkward tangents, dead space
issues.fix: Raise the camera target so the board sits centred with about 8% margin all round, lower the FOV to around 35°, and fill the backdrop with room or table context

issues.problem: Browser-default Times New Roman and the system button font, a single size with no scale steps, and proportional digits in the score line.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 8 ≤5: fallback fonts, random sizes; task note: browser-default fonts ≤5
issues.fix: Load a rounded display face (e.g. Fredoka 600) for headings and Nunito 700 for the UI, set a scale of 16/24/32/48, and add font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to the scores

issues.problem: Unstyled default HTML buttons, about 20 px tall, with 1 px grey borders, no radius system and no shadows. The HUD is raw text with no panel.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 9 ≤5: default controls
issues.fix: Style the buttons as pills (radius 16 px, padding 12×24, 4-pt spacing, 0 4px 0 darker-shade shadow, hover and pressed states) and put the HUD in a rounded paper card with 16 px padding

issues.problem: The board is a flat light-grey plane with 1 px grid lines, and there is no material read anywhere (no wood, felt or paper grain).
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 10: surfaces read as materials
issues.fix: Apply a wood-grain albedo plus a normal map to the board frame and a felt texture with subtle noise to the playfield, draw the grid as inlaid grooves, and give the background a tinted wall or table surface

issues.region: top-right green vs top-left red pieces
issues.problem: Players are told apart only by hue, and red vs green is the exact pairing that fails deuteranopia. There are no glyphs or shapes. The black 16 px text is also small against the mid-grey.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 11 ≤5: players distinguishable only by red vs green
issues.fix: Give each player a unique glyph on the piece tops (circle/triangle/square/star) and a different piece silhouette, pick hues that differ in luminance, and put the HUD text on a panel with ≥4.5:1 contrast

issues.problem: It reads instantly as an engine prototype or template (grey primitives, default fonts and buttons). A stranger would not believe it's a premium indie game.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 15 ≤5: looks like a prototype
issues.fix: Address items 1, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9 together: a unified material set, a harmonised palette, soft shadowed lighting, rounded toy forms, a custom type system and styled UI cards

issues.problem: The room code is small default body text, identical to the other lines, so a viewer can't pick it out at a glance. There is no audience UI or timer.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 17: room code legible, audience UI clear
issues.fix: Put the room code in a dedicated badge in the top-right (monospace-free display font ≥28 px at 1080p, letter-spacing 0.1em, high-contrast chip) with a 'join at' URL beneath it

issues.problem: Visible aliasing and stair-stepping on the thin grid lines and the die/board edges suggest MSAA is off, and the grid lines break up toward the far edge.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 18: no aliasing shimmer
issues.fix: Enable antialias:true on the renderer (or an SMAA pass), set pixelRatio to min(devicePixelRatio, 2), and bake the grid into a mipmapped texture with anisotropy 8 instead of using line primitives

issues.problem: Default grey three.js-style materials on the board, background, die and sphere, plus primitive cylinders, serif browser text and stock HTML buttons. Nothing suggests a crafted clay, wood or paper world, and no single art direction ties the elements together.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 1 '≤ 5: mixed styles, default grey three.js materials, stock widgets'; §4.1 anchor 5
issues.fix: Replace the default MeshStandard grey with authored materials (a warm wood mat and a felt or paper board with painted squares). Model the pieces as chunky toy pawns, style the HUD as paper or wood cards and set the scene in a lit room instead of the #808080 void.

issues.problem: Turn, room code and scores sit in roughly 16px black serif text crammed in the top-left corner with no panel. At 720p JPEG you would have to squint to read them. Nothing on the board marks whose turn it is, and the Player 2 identity is not colour-linked to a piece set.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 2 '10: turn, state and scores clear within 1 s; critical text ≥ 22 px'; '≤ 5: squinting required'
issues.fix: Move the turn state into a prominent top-centre banner at ≥ 32px at 1080p, with a player-coloured plate. Show scores as four identity-coloured chips of ≥ 24px, and highlight the active player's pieces with a rim glow.

issues.problem: The players are pure primary colours: saturated #0000CC-like blue, neon #00CC00 green, pure red and mustard yellow. They sit on a neutral grey board and background with ungraded grey shading, the text is pure black and the button fills are pure white. Nothing harmonises the hues.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 3 '≤ 5: off-palette, grey shadows, neon'; §4.1 anchor 5 'primary colours'
issues.fix: Retune the player colours to a harmonised, desaturated set (e.g. terracotta, sage, dusty blue, honey). Tint the shadows warm-purple, replace #000 and #FFF with ink and cream tones, and give the background a warm gradient.

issues.problem: The lighting is flat and ambient-heavy. There are no cast or blob shadows, so the pieces do not lift off the board, and there is no rim light and no key light direction. There is also no mood or mode identity.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 4 '≤ 5: flat or harsh lighting'
issues.fix: Add a warm directional key light from the upper left at about 45°, soft shadow maps or blob shadows under the pieces, a cool fill light and a subtle rim light. Add a tinted environment or hemisphere light to set the mood.

issues.problem: The die is a sharp unbeveled box, the pieces are plain hard-edged cylinders and the board is a razor-thin flat plane with sharp corners. Nothing has the rounded, chunky toy form.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 5 '≤ 5: sharp boxes, spindly shapes'
issues.fix: Use a RoundedBoxGeometry die with a radius of about 0.15 of its size and pips. Bevel the piece tops and turn them into rounded pawn silhouettes, and give the board a thick rounded-edge frame.

issues.problem: There is no focal point. The unlabelled sphere and die in the centre are ambiguous, the corner piece groups compete equally for attention, and the call to action (Roll) is a tiny stock button in the bottom-right corner.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 6 '≤ 5: unclear call to action'
issues.fix: Make the Roll action a large player-coloured button, bottom-centre, at ≥ 64px height. Spotlight the active player's corner and die, and dim the inactive pieces to about 70% value.

issues.problem: The board floats in a flat grey void, with a large dead band above it and nothing framing the scene. The HUD and buttons hug the extreme corners with almost no padding.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 7 '≤ 5: dead space'
issues.fix: Lower the camera pitch and tighten the FOV so the board fills about 75% of the width, with a table or room context behind it. Inset the HUD by at least 24px safe margins.

issues.problem: The HUD uses the browser-default serif (Times) and the buttons use a system sans. There is no scale hierarchy (all lines are the same size) and no designed typeface.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 8 '≤ 5: fallback fonts, random sizes'
issues.fix: Load a rounded display face for headings and a humanist sans for body text. Use a scale of 32/24/18px with tabular numerals for the scores.

issues.problem: Roll and End turn are unstyled default HTML buttons: grey 1px border, no radius and no shadow. The HUD text has no container or padding.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 9 '≤ 5: default controls'
issues.fix: Style the buttons with a 12px radius, a soft tinted drop shadow, 16/24px padding and hover and pressed states. Wrap the HUD in a card on a 4pt spacing grid.

issues.problem: The board is untextured flat light grey with hairline grid lines. It reads as no material at all: no wood, felt or paper, and no grain.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 10 '10: wood, felt, paper read as materials'
issues.fix: Apply a painted wood or felt albedo with subtle grain and a normal map. Draw the squares as inked or inlaid tiles instead of 1px lines.

issues.problem: The red and green players are told apart only by hue. There is no glyph or shape identity, so they merge under deuteranopia or protanopia. The score text also refers to P1–P4 without linking them to colours.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 11 '≤ 5: players distinguishable only by red vs green'
issues.fix: Give each player a unique glyph and pawn shape (circle, triangle, square, star), shift the colours apart in luminance, and show each glyph next to its score in the HUD.

issues.problem: At a glance this reads as a technical prototype or template, not a premium indie game. Grey void, primitives, default fonts and stock buttons all contribute.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 15 '≤ 5: looks like a prototype, demo or template'
issues.fix: Carry out an art pass per issues CAL-R1-01, 03, 04, 05, 08 and 09: authored materials, a harmonised palette, warm key lighting, rounded forms, a designed font and styled UI.

issues.problem: The room code is small plain serif text with no emphasis. There is no join URL, no audience affordance (poll, odds) and no timer.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 17 '10: room code legible'; '≤ 5: audience state invisible or confusing'
issues.fix: Show the room code in a dedicated pill of ≥ 28px with letter-spacing and a join URL, placed in a stream-safe corner, plus an audience panel for polls and the timer.

issues.problem: The 1px grid lines alias and stair-step in perspective, and the die and board silhouettes have jagged edges. No anti-aliasing is visible.

issues.problem: The frame reads as premium indie, but the uniform facade row and the large empty sky make it a little less considered than the board's stronger compositions.

issues.problem: Bubble tails taper to fairly sharp points, unlike the chunky rounded forms everywhere else.

issues.problem: Two equal-weight bubbles split the focus; nothing marks which one is ahead.

issues.problem: Slight banding in the green radial glow gradient.

issues.problem: The glossy yellow serif prompt with a hard dark drop shadow looks like broadcast-graphics type, not handmade clay or paper like the rest of the frame.
